newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse blues braked by bonds, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse blues braked by bonds, Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed on Thursday with lighter losses than had been earlier foreseen thanks to gains on Wall Street and the bond market.
Dealers said the session's slippage was due to profit taking and the short term outlook remained bright. Attention was next expected to shift to September CPI data due on Friday.
The general index lost 0.80 points, 0.22 percent, to 371.15 and the Ibex-35 fell 10.30 points, 0.24 percent, to 4,247.48.
"The market continues to have a strong foundation and it's normal for it to produce some profit-taking," one dealer said.

Trading volume picked up in late trade after some technical gliches earlier and there were two big block trades by BBV Interactivos, one for 75,650 Banco Popular shares and the other for 658,000 Fecsa shares.

Much of the session's trading was focused on the electricity sector after reports of a possible increase in Endesa's participation in Fecsa and Sevillana, which gained 1.15 percent and 1.3 percent respectively. Endesa rose 10 pesetas to 7,500.
Telefonica lost five pesetas to 2,465 with 3.1 million shares traded.
